rules.accepted_credit_types: At least 30 hours AMA or AOA Category 1 (ACCME, state medical association or AOA CCME accredited sponsors); remainder Category I or II (self-instruction, consultation, databases, patient care review, teaching, publications, etc.)
rules.alternatives: Instead of the 60 hours: a recognized specialty organization CME certification in effect at renewal; passing an ABMS or AOA board (re)certification exam (= 60 hours); accredited postgraduate training (50 h per full-time year). State-specific courses (HB 1, domestic violence, pediatric abusive head trauma) still apply. No waivers; retired physicians with active licenses must comply.
rules.audit_note: Compliance confirmed on the annual renewal form at the end of each 3-year cycle; random audit after April 1 following the cycle. Extension request by April 1 ($100); non-compliance fine at least $200 and 6 months to comply, then suspension.

topics.who: Physicians authorized to prescribe or dispense controlled substances in Kentucky; Board-approved HB 1 CME each 3-year cycle
Pediatricians, radiologists, family practitioners, emergency medicine and urgent care physicians: Board-approved pediatric abusive head trauma training
Primary care physicians licensed after July 1, 1996, within 3 years of initial licensure

rules.notes: One board for MDs and DOs. CME runs in 3-year calendar cycles ending Dec 31; licenses renew annually. The Board CME page still cites the 2018-2020 cycle and an amendment to 201 KAR 9:310 is pending, so check current cycle dates.
